<think>**Designing explicit one-hot decoder**

</think>

{
  "candidate_rtl": "module mux_large (
    input [7:0] block_a, block_b, block_c, block_d, block_e,
    input [7:0] block_f, block_g, block_h, block_i, block_j,
    input [3:0] sel,
    output reg [7:0] block_out
);

    wire en_a, en_b, en_c, en_d, en_e;
    wire en_f, en_g, en_h, en_i, en_j;

    // Explicitly decode the default selection without a priority chain.
    assign en_a = (~|sel) | (sel[3] & (sel[2] | sel[1]));
    assign en_b = (sel == 4'd1);
    assign en_c = (sel == 4'd2);
    assign en_d = (sel == 4'd3);
    assign en_e = (sel == 4'd4);
    assign en_f = (sel == 4'd5);
    assign en_g = (sel == 4'd6);
    assign en_h = (sel == 4'd7);
    assign en_i = (sel == 4'd8);
    assign en_j = (sel == 4'd9);

    always @* begin
        block_out = ({8{en_a}} & block_a)
                  | ({8{en_b}} & block_b)
                  | ({8{en_c}} & block_c)
                  | ({8{en_d}} & block_d)
                  | ({8{en_e}} & block_e)
                  | ({8{en_f}} & block_f)
                  | ({8{en_g}} & block_g)
                  | ({8{en_h}} & block_h)
                  | ({8{en_i}} & block_i)
                  | ({8{en_j}} & block_j);
    end
endmodule
",
  "bottleneck": "The supplied baseline has select-to-output critical paths containing select decoding, buffering and several combining stages. Its maximum reported data arrival is 1.04 ns. The default-selection logic is a plausible contributor, but the supplied paths do not establish an exact gate-to-RTL correspondence.",
  "rewrite": "Replace the case/default representation with an explicit one-hot masked OR. Decode block_a directly as sel=0 or sel>=10, rather than expressing its enable as the complement of the nine other selections. This exposes parallel selection logic and permits ABC to map the data combination into NAND/NOR and compound cells without an explicit final default-data mux.",
  "expected_timing_gain": "Hypothesis only: simplifying the default enable and exposing parallel masking may reduce select-to-output depth relative to the 1.04 ns baseline. No candidate timing measurement is available; neither a positive gain nor minimum achievable mapped arrival is established.",
  "area_or_other_cost": "The implementation shares ten enables across eight data bits. Decode fanout, OR-network mapping and buffering may offset the intended timing benefit. Candidate area has not been measured, so compliance with the 1006.089920 um^2 cap is not certified. Yosys/OpenSTA execution was not available here: complete source and mapped equivalence proofs and zero max-slew/max-capacitance violations have not been obtained. This is therefore an unvalidated candidate, not a result satisfying those mandatory acceptance checks.",
  "functional_boundaries": "Preserves the module interface and uses only synthesizable Verilog-2001 combinational logic. For two-state inputs, en_a is true exactly for sel=0 and sel=10..15; en_b through en_j are true exactly for sel=1..9 respectively. Consequently exactly one mask is active for every selector value, and each output bit equals the corresponding selected input bit regardless of all 80 data bits. No state, latency, assumptions or don't-cares are introduced. This exhaustive selector argument establishes the intended source-level Boolean equivalence, but is not a substitute for the requested tool-generated source and mapped equivalence proofs. Four-state X/Z equivalence is not claimed."
}
